(1) the use of HPGs in feedlot finishing of beef steers has a negative effect, as measured by objective testing, and (2) the use of these implants has a negative effect as measured by consumer preference.
the use of hormone growth promotant implants in steers negatively affects beef palatability as assessed by objective testing (Warmer-Bratzler) and by consumer sensory testing.
the use of growth-promoting hormones has a negative effect upon beef palatability, as measured by objective tests and consumer preference.

the question: "Is there a negative effect on the beef industry of the widespread use of HGP in cattle?"
the effects of hormone growth promotants (HGPs) on beef quality, and in particular with the effects of HGPs on palatability.

the use of these implants is associated with a reduction in beef palatability, but that this reduction is not sufficient to be of practical significance to the beef consumer.
the use of hormone implants is a negative factor in the production of beef with high palatability.
the use of implants in steers is not justified on the basis of palatability.

the use of HGPs has a negative effect, albeit small, on beef palatablility.
